title: EU and UK hold a rare summit in bid to 'rebuild ties'
summary: European Union officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham met in Brussels to discuss efforts to rebuild ties following Brexit.

image.caption: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is seeking to mend build closer ties with the EU after BrexitImage: Yves Herman/REUTERS

blocks.text: European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham were set to announce deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.
This might be the first steps to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.

In September, Burnham said he would seek a political consensus on the country's future relationship with the EU, even suggesting he could campaign to take Britain back into the bloc at the next election.
What did Burnham say at the EU-UK summit?
Brussels said the agreements would only take effect if a deal is reached to lower university tuition fees for EU students studying in the UK.

"Britain and Europe share values, interests and a global neighborhood. In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together. A closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe," Burnham said as he arrived in Brussels.
UK prime minister, who was greeted on arrival by a string quintet, said Britain should explore different options for its future relationship with the EU, including rejoining the bloc.
On Monday, he said it ​was the "obvious truth" that ‌Britain had lost more than it had gained from Brexit.

Three key agreements were being discussed in Brussels: one to simplify food exports by reducing red tape, another to link the UK and EU emissions-trading systems, and a third to establish a "youth experience scheme."

It aims to facilitate British companies exporting food to Europe, as well as enabling young people to travel between the UK and EU for work and study without being subject to existing visa requirements.

A key obstacle was securing a commitment from the UK to reach a future agreement that would reduce university tuition fees for EU students to the same level paid by British students. The EU made the implementation of the other agreements conditional on reaching such a deal.
The two sides had agreed on these initiatives shortly before the summit started, DPA news agency reported, citing EU diplomats and officials.

According to DPA, the agreements will only take effect if both sides reach a deal to lower tuition fees for EU students at British universities. They aim to reach an agreement on this issue within the next six months.

Speaking to AP news agency, a British government spokesperson said "the deal is done," adding that details would be published in a joint statement later.
Polling firm YouGov runs a regular tracker on whether the UK was right or wrong to vote to quit.
Since mid-2022, a majority of people surveyed said Britain was wrong to leave.In September, the "Bregret" camp rose to 60% — the highest ever.
